Also: when did the severe lower abdominal pain and shortness of breath start (sudden vs gradual), and do you have any fever/chills or inability to pass urine/gas?

message.content:
The catheter we’re talking about is a urinary catheter that was placed **inside my continent MAINZ pouch** (the internal reservoir we use after my bladder was removed). It was put in so the pouch could drain continuously because I’d been having increasing trouble catheterising it on my own.

The drainage stopped the night before I came to the emergency department, and **that night the severe lower‑abdominal pain began and the shortness of breath got worse**. It wasn’t an instant “sharp” hit; the pain and the breathing trouble built up gradually after the catheter stopped working.

I haven’t noticed any fever or chills, and I don’t recall any new problems passing gas or urine beyond the reduced output from the pouch that I mentioned. (Those details weren’t brought up in my story.)

The patient has a continent MAINZ pouch I urinary diversion after radical cystectomy. So catheter is likely a catheter placed into the continent pouch (urinary catheter). It was placed for continuous drainage of the pouch because catheterizing difficulty. So answer: urinary catheter into the pouch.

Timing: severe lower abdominal pain and progressive dyspnea followed catheter dysfunction. So after drainage failed the night before presentation. So pain started after that, likely gradual progressive. No mention of fever/chills or inability to pass urine/gas. So say not mentioned. Also ask about fever/chills: not reported.
